article.headline: Liberty spoils Bird's WNBA debut

images.name: Bird, Sue 020530 inline
images.caption: Sue Bird's WNBA debut was a mixed bag, with 18 points, six assists, five turnovers and a loss.

article.linkText: Liberty beat Storm, spoil Bird's WNBA debut
article.story:
SEATTLE (AP) -- The New York Liberty didn't get Sue Bird, so they spoiled her WNBA debut. Bird, the league's overall No. 1 draft pick, scored a game-high 18 points but had an uncharacteristic five turnovers as the Liberty ruined Seattle's season opener, beating the Storm 78-61 Thursday night. "I watched Sue Bird at Connecticut for the last two years and know she's a great player,'' Liberty coach Richie Adubato said. "She looked even more terrific tonight. I just wish she was in New York.'' Crystal Robinson led the Liberty with 17 points and three steals as New York shot above 50 percent for the second night in a row. "I really didn't think about Sue Bird,'' Robinson said. Bird, who led undefeated Connecticut to the NCAA championship last season, scored 11 points in the second half. She was 5-of-12 from the field, had six assists and three steals. "Whatever, we lost,'' she said. "It doesn't really matter.'' Losing is new for Bird, who has won at every level since she played youth basketball. "At times she looked like a rookie, and at times she looked like an all-pro,'' Seattle coach Lin Dunn said. "We need to get her turnovers down to two max a game.'' Tamika Whitmore had 14 points and Tari Phillips and Vickie Johnson each added 13 for the Liberty (2-1). Rookie reserve Felicia Ragland had 15 points for the Storm, while Semeka Randall added 13. Seattle played without center Lauren Jackson, its leading scorer last season, who sprained her right ankle in practice Sunday. The 6-foot-5 Jackson, the WNBA's top draft pick last season and an All-Star as a rookie, is questionable for Sunday's game at Portland. Robinson had two 3-pointers during a 9-0 run in the first half that gave the Liberty a 25-12 lead at 10:53. Seattle then scored 10 straight points, including six by Ragland, to pull within 25-22. New York's Sue Wicks was called for a technical foul during that stretch for slamming the ball to the floor when she was called for a foul, and Ragland converted the free throw. The Liberty outscored the Storm 11-4 over the final 4:36 for a 36-26 halftime lead. New York shot 56 percent in the first half and 50.9 for the game after making 54 percent of its shots in an 84-62 win in Portland on Wednesday. "When we execute our offense, we're very hard to stop,'' Robinson said. "They pushed the ball and pressed. They have young legs and a lot of energy and our guards handled it like veterans.'' Seattle finished 19-for-60 from the field (31.7 percent).

Game notes
Sonics All-Star Gary Payton attended the game, sitting in the front row courtside, just down from Sonics and Storm owner Howard Schultz, the chairman of Starbucks Coffee Co. ... Bird took the first shot of the game, missing a 3-pointer. She then scored Seattle's first points, driving through the key for a left-handed layup at 18:33. She was unhappy with her turnovers. "There's no excuse for that,'' she said. "It's just careless.'' ... The Liberty have won all three meetings with the Storm. They won the first two by a total of 37 points.
